an0586.user: YouTube, last 30 days, snacks brand. Impressions 12.1L, clicks 11,245, CTR 0.9%, orders 133, conversion rate 1.18%, AOV ₹1,600. Running broad-match keywords. What's wrong here?

Low CTR on YouTube isn't your problem; you're getting clicks. The problem is what kind of clicks. Broad-match keywords are pulling in people who typed something loosely related and are wandering, not hunting for a snack to buy right now. High reach, low intent — you're paying for browsers.

The proof is in the gap: clicks are healthy but only 1.18% of those clickers buy. If this were a creative or page problem you'd see it bite earlier; instead it's the audience composition leaking value at the very end.

The one lever: kill broad-match. Tighten to high-intent keywords and audiences — in-market for snacks/D2C food, custom-intent off competitor and category searches — and load a real negative-keyword list to choke off the junk queries eating your budget. Optimise for purchases, not clicks; the click metric has been flattering you.

One caveat: 133 orders is a usable but not huge sample. Make the targeting change, then judge it on the next ~100+ conversions before declaring victory — don't read week one as the verdict.
